text:
IncidentBot: Alert: p99 latency spike detected for ingress-lb(eu-west-2) — streaming stalls observed, SLO breach window started at 2026-02-12T09:14:48Z. Paging on-call (rotation: Maya R).
Maya R: I'm on it, grabbing paged logs and checking LB health. @Priya_S are we seeing any deploys? :eyes:
Priya S: no deploys in last 30m. Nothing in Canary pipeline. I see increased 502/504s from edge metrics and connection resets from a subset of backends.
Alan C: also seeing routing table churn on the router service; hash distribution shows one shard with 60% of new flows. Probably a hot-shard.
Maya R: ok — what is customer impact? CustomerOps, any inbound tickets?
CustomerOps: two large customers reported streaming stalls (websocket disconnect + re-establish) and elevated p99. They flagged timeouts in the same timeframe. No data exfil or errors beyond timeouts.
Jorge L: dumping recent routing-policy changes: last change was a weight rebalancing job at 08:55 UTC that adjusted zone weights for cost-optimizations. Rolling back that policy might be quickest mitigation.
Maya R: can we temporarily force traffic away from the affected shard/zone? We have ejection rules available. What's the healthcheck rate on that shard?
Alan C: healthchecks mostly green but tail retries are high. I suspect misrouting: LB policy sends new streaming sessions to a subset of routers that have an elongated KV cache miss pattern, causing long warmups.
Priya S: confirmed: KV cache miss rate for that router group spiked 10x around 09:10. Streaming stall timelines line up with new session creation.
Maya R: Plan A: eject the problematic zone from LB for 10m and reroute to fallback zone; Plan B: rollback weight change; Plan C: add short warmup tolerance and increase batching. Start with Plan A so minimal code risk.
Alan C: I'll apply a temporary zone ejection via the control plane. Command: 
```
# eject zone euw2a for 10m
redwoodctl lb ejection create --zone euw2a --duration 10m --reason "tail-latency spike"
```
Maya R: execute when ready. Notify if we see traffic shifting and p99 drops.
DeployBot: LB ejection request queued (job id: 84821).
Alan C: job executed, ejection active. Traffic shunted to euw2b/c.
Maya R: metrics update — p95 improved from 420ms -> 190ms in 2m, p99 still high at ~1.5s but trending down. Streaming retry rate down 40%.
Priya S: playback traces show fewer cold KV cache misses after ejection. Good sign.
CustomerOps: telling the two customers we applied a mitigation and are monitoring; suspects reduced impact.
Jorge L: quick postmortem note — weight rebalance moved a large fraction of new flows to euw2a, which doesn't have warmed caches for long-running streaming variants (session affinity was preserved so cold clients funneled). That explains stalls.
Maya R: still seeing isolated tail spikes. Could be a combination of hot partition + misrouted long-lived connections. We'll keep ejection for the full 10m and prepare rollback for the weight change if needed.
Alan C: preparing rollback patch for the weight job (dry-run ready). If p99 doesn't get below 800ms after ejection window, we roll back.
Maya R: also enabling higher-resolution tracing for affected routers for the next 15m (low overhead sampling ramp).
Priya S: side note: streaming clients are sensitive to early rebalances — need to ensure session affinity or warm start for streaming route variants. Adding an action item.
Maya R: update at +7m: p99 980ms -> 720ms -> trending. Some customers still seeing occasional stalls, but overall error budget hit probability decreased.
Jorge L: adding alert correlation: same timeframe shows a spike in continuous-batching fallback in the runtime logs — routers fell back to synchronous path under pressure, increasing token latency for streaming.
Maya R: ok. After ejection expires, we'll do a controlled rollback of the weight-change to restore balanced distribution but keep an eye on cache-warmth. Alan — schedule rollback job now but don't execute until we agree.
Alan C: rollback job scheduled (job id: 84822), awaiting manual trigger.
CustomerOps: we'll keep customers updated; prepping a short post-incident note for status page.
Maya R: final note for oncall handoff — if p99 goes >1200ms for more than 3m, escalate to SRE lead + platform eng for live mitigation. Leaving monitoring to Priya for the next 15m and then handing to Alan for overnight.
Priya S: will monitor and paste key traces here.
Maya R: thanks team — holding this thread open. :thumbsup:
---
(15 minutes later)
Priya S: after ejection expired, p99 stabilized ~350ms after we triggered the scheduled rollback (we executed the rollback at +12m because residual skew remained). No further stalls in the next 8m.
Maya R: closing mitigation window. Action items: 1) add pre-warm for streaming route types before weight shifts, 2) add LB policy test gating for large weight deltas, 3) run a chaos test for ejection handling, 4) post-incident writeup.
Jorge L: adding action item: telemetry to surface new-flow hotness by session type.
CustomerOps: drafting customer comms now; will share.
Maya R: handoff to Alan for overnight watch. Alan, you're oncall for the next shift.
Alan C: thanks, taking over. I'll post a short summary to the incidents channel and tag SRE lead for the writeup.
IncidentBot: Incident resolved: mitigation applied, SLO trending back to normal. Incident window closed at 2026-02-12T09:46:28Z.
Maya R: nice job everyone.
